The code path that drives\n  this is `onGroupUnloaded`, specifically the `PreparingRebalance` branch that iterates\n  `group.allMemberMetadata` and calls `group.maybeInvokeJoinCallback`.\n\n  No test exercises `onResignation` while a `JoinGroup` future is still parked in the purgatory.\n  The only related test (`testRequestHandlingWhileLoadingInProgress`) only covers *loading*, not\n  *unloading*, and only for requests that arrive after the fact.\n\n- **Proposed Test**:\n  ```scala\n  @Test\n  def testOnGroupUnloadedDuringPreparingRebalanceReturnsNotCoordinator(): Unit = {\n    // Put one member into a stable group first.\n    val firstJoinResult = dynamicJoinGroup(groupId, JoinGroupRequest.UNKNOWN_MEMBER_ID,\n      protocolType, protocols)\n    val firstMemberId = firstJoinResult.memberId\n    EasyMock.reset(replicaManager)\n    val firstSyncResult = syncGroupLeader(groupId, firstJoinResult.generationId,\n      firstMemberId, Map(firstMemberId -> Array[Byte]()))\n    assertEquals(Errors.NONE, firstSyncResult.error)\n\n    // Trigger a rebalance by having the leader re-join; this parks a Future.\n    EasyMock.reset(replicaManager)\n    val rejoinFuture = sendJoinGroup(groupId, firstMemberId, protocolType, protocols)\n    assertGroupState(groupState = PreparingRebalance)\n\n    // Simulate coordinator partition resignation while the rebalance is pending.\n    groupCoordinator.onResignation(groupPartitionId, Some(1))\n\n    // The pending JoinGroup callback must have fired with NOT_COORDINATOR.\n    val rejoinResult = Await.result(rejoinFuture, Duration(1, TimeUnit.MILLISECONDS))\n    assertEquals(Errors.NOT_COORDINATOR, rejoinResult.error)\n\n    // Group metadata should now be Dead and removed.\n    assertGroupState(groupId, groupState = Dead)\n  }\n  ```\n- **Coverage Delta**: Exercises `onGroupUnloaded` → `PreparingRebalance` branch\n  (`maybeInvokeJoinCallback` with `NOT_COORDINATOR`), `rebalancePurgatory.checkAndComplete`,\n  and `removeSyncExpiration`.  Also implicitly tests that `onResignation` → `removeGroupsForPartition`\n  → `onGroupUnloaded` are wired correctly.\n\n---\n\n### Failure Mode 2: Over-Capacity Group Forces Rebalance on Load\n\n- **Risk**: HIGH\n- **Code Location**: `GroupCoordinator.scala` ~lines 1124–1134 (`onGroupLoaded`)\n- **Description**: `onGroupLoaded` contains an explicit check:\n\n  ```scala\n  if (groupIsOverCapacity(group)) {\n    prepareRebalance(group, ...)\n  }\n  ```\n\n  This fires when the operator reduces `group.max.session.timeout.ms` / `group.max.size` and\n  a previously larger group is loaded on a new coordinator epoch.  No test constructs a group\n  whose size exceeds `groupConfig.groupMaxSize` and then calls `onGroupLoaded` (via `onElection`).\n\n- **Proposed Test**:\n  ```scala\n  @Test\n  def testOnGroupLoadedOverCapacityTriggersRebalance(): Unit = {\n    // Build a group with GroupMaxSize+1 members directly in Stable state.\n    val overCapacityGroup = new GroupMetadata(groupId, Stable, new MockTime())\n    val extraMemberCount = GroupMaxSize + 1\n    val memberIds = (1 to extraMemberCount).map { i =>\n      overCapacityGroup.generateMemberId(ClientId, None)\n    }\n    memberIds.foreach { memberId =>\n      val member = new MemberMetadata(memberId, None, ClientId, ClientHost,\n        DefaultRebalanceTimeout, DefaultSessionTimeout, protocolType, protocols)\n      overCapacityGroup.add(member)\n    }\n    groupCoordinator.groupManager.addGroup(overCapacityGroup)\n    assertTrue(overCapacityGroup.is(Stable))\n    assertEquals(extraMemberCount, overCapacityGroup.size)\n\n    // Simulate the coordinator loading the partition owning this group.\n    // onGroupLoaded is the internal callback wired through scheduleLoadGroupAndOffsets.\n    groupCoordinator.onElection(groupPartitionId, coordinatorEpoch = 1)\n    // Give the scheduler a chance to process the load event.\n    timer.advanceClock(1)\n\n    // Group must now be in PreparingRebalance because it exceeded max size.\n    assertGroupState(groupState = PreparingRebalance)\n  }\n  ```\n- **Coverage Delta**: The only code path reaching `onGroupLoaded → groupIsOverCapacity → prepareRebalance`\n  is exercised.  Also exercises the `onElection → scheduleLoadGroupAndOffsets → onGroupLoaded` chain.\n\n---\n\n### Failure Mode 3: Standalone Offset Commit on Non-Empty Group Returns UNKNOWN_MEMBER_ID\n\n- **Risk**: MEDIUM\n- **Code Location**: `GroupCoordinator.scala` ~lines 969–974 (`validateOffsetCommit`)\n- **Description**: When `generationId < 0 AND memberId == UNKNOWN_MEMBER_ID AND groupInstanceId`\n  is None **but the group is not Empty**, `validateOffsetCommit` returns\n  `Some(Errors.UNKNOWN_MEMBER_ID)`.  This prevents external tools from silently clobbering\n  offsets for a live consumer group.\n\n  The existing `testCommitOffsetWithDefaultGeneration` and `testCommitOffsetsAfterGroupIsEmpty`\n  only cover the case where the group does not yet exist (i.e., `getGroup` returns `None`) or is\n  already `Empty`.  // Must be rejected because the group is non-empty.\n    assertEquals(Errors.UNKNOWN_MEMBER_ID, commitResult(tp))\n\n    // Original offset must not have been changed.\n    val (fetchErr, partData) = groupCoordinator.handleFetchOffsets(groupId,\n      requireStable = false, Some(Seq(tp)))\n    assertEquals(Errors.NONE, fetchErr)\n    assertEquals(Some(OffsetFetchResponse.INVALID_OFFSET),
